newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Most Shanghai copper futures contracts ended slightly down on Friday on profit-taking triggered by overnight fluctuations on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,770 yuan ($2,865) per tonne, losing 20 yuan. It opened down at 23,650 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,630 and a high of 23,780.
March, the only contract to rise, put on 20 yuan to 23,400. April fell 30 to 23,620, May 50 to 23,720, July 10 to 23,740, and August 80 to 23,700.
Combined volume fell to 37,730 tonnes from 72,590.
Copper opened lower but buying at low levels pushed prices from lows for the rest of the session.
"Profit-taking prevented copper from rising further today, but volume dropped sharply, indicating many investors are holding on to their positions," one trader said.
"Consolidation at high levels after sharp gains over the past few days did not discourage long position holders," he added.
Traders said copper prices were not likely to fall sharply as the peak consumption season approaches.
But some traders said recent consolidation indicated institutional buyers were liquidating their long positions and taking profits.
"Fundamentals for the whole year are not optimistic, it can not support long-term rises," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended mostly up. March rose 20 yuan to 15,900, April was unchanged at 16,200, May put on 50 to 16,600 and June rose 50 to 16,800.
Combined volume fell to 2,010 tonnes from 6,810.
